title: Release plan + rollout checklist for hardware tuning profiles pack
creator: Talia Benson
description:
Release readiness ticket for the hardware tuning profiles pack. Owns final checklist, comms to SRE/oncall/Support, rollout/rollback criteria, and explicit sign-offs required to ship the pack in runtime-1.18 (Hosted + Dedicated) with Private enablement via Helm values. Also defines B200 experimental gating + pool/region rollout constraints.

Key outcomes:
- Single source of truth checklist for “ship” and “rollback” decisions
- Concrete rollout schedule by environment (perf canary -> internal -> Hosted low-risk pools -> Dedicated -> Private)
- Comms plan (eng-oncall, eng-sre, Support/CS) + links to runbooks/dashboards
- Final sign-off list and what each org is signing off on
acceptance_criteria:
1) Release checklist is complete, reviewed, and approved by Runtime + SRE + Infra.
2) Rollout plan includes: phases, who pushes the button, monitoring windows, and rollback procedure per phase.
3) Rollback criteria are numerical (p95/p99 deltas, error rate, OOM rate, queue saturation), not “judgment calls”.
4) Comms are sent (or scheduled) to eng-oncall and eng-sre with links to dashboards/runbooks + how to disable per pool.
5) Private enablement instructions and override order are explicitly stated (Helm values, env var overrides, and safe defaults).
6) B200 profile remains gated behind experimental flag; enabling requires explicit approval + limited pools and documented fallback.

Release packaging assumptions (as of runtime-1.18 RC):
- H100 profile: ON by default for Hosted + Dedicated H100 pools after staged rollout (starting with “balanced” preset)
- L40S profile: ON by default for Hosted + Dedicated L40S pools (guardrails enabled; conservative KV cache budgeting)
- B200 profile: OFF by default globally; available only with feature flag + allowlisted pools; auto-fallback to H100-compatible baseline if detection/compat fails

Operational controls that must exist before rollout:
- Per-pool disable switch (config override) that reverts to baseline defaults without a redeploy
- Visibility: metric emitted for selected_profile + override_source + key knob deltas (from pr-22027)
- Startup log line printing runtime version + profile pack version + compatibility matrix (pr-22041)
- CLI to dump effective runtime config for triage (pr-22066)
rollout_plan:
Phased rollout (targeting runtime-1.18):

Phase 0: Pre-merge / pre-release gating (CI + perf-canary)
- Scope: Every PR that modifies profile pack, loader, scheduler defaults, kernel selection, or KV cache budgets.
- Gates (minimum):
  - p50 latency: <= +3% vs baseline
  - p95 latency: <= +5% vs baseline (streaming and non-streaming tracked separately)
  - tokens/sec: >= -2% vs baseline (or explicit waiver with documented trade-off)
  - error rate (5xx + timeouts): <= +0.1pp absolute
  - OOM / CUDA errors: no increase (0 tolerance in canary)
- Owner: Kira Volkov + Aisha Bello
- Artifact: standardized benchmark summary (benchmark-lab/pr-1842 output)

Phase 1: Internal canary pools (Hosted)
- Duration: minimum 24h monitoring window per GPU SKU
- Pools: 1 low-traffic region per SKU (H100 + L40S), then 2nd region if stable
- Action: enable profile pack with explicit version pin; do not allow overrides except “disable all profiles”
- Owner: Vanessa Ortiz (fleet change) + Sean Gallagher (oncall readiness)

Phase 2: Hosted gradual ramp
- Ramp: 5% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% of eligible traffic by pool (or by node allocation if traffic splitting isn’t available)
- Hold points: minimum 2 hours at 5/25/50% during business hours; overnight only if green + oncall notified
- Success criteria: sustained improvement or neutrality in p95 with >= +5% tokens/sec on representative routes OR documented acceptance of neutral performance with improved stability/cost

Phase 3: Dedicated pools (new nodes first)
- Approach: profile pack enabled only on newly provisioned nodes for first week; existing nodes unchanged unless customer opts in
- Customer comms: “no API changes; only runtime tuning; expected behavior documented; rollback available per pool”
- Owner: Irene Choi + Customer Success partner (via Support runbook)

Phase 4: Private enablement
- Ship mechanism: Helm values support (helm-charts/pr-612) + runtime compatibility logs
- Default: OFF unless customer sets values; documentation points to safe presets and supported overrides
- Support posture: require customer to provide effective config dump output for triage (pr-22066)

B200 special case (experimental):
- Only Phase 1 (internal canary) + limited Phase 2 in explicitly approved pool(s)
- Requires explicit go/no-go from Runtime sponsor + SRE sponsor; no weekend rollout
- Auto-disable if driver/CUDA version checks fail; must log the reason and fall back
rollback_criteria:
Rollback is mandatory if any of the below occurs within the monitoring window AND is attributable to the profile-enabled build/preset (or cannot be ruled out quickly):

Hard rollback triggers (immediate):
- p99 latency regression >= +15% sustained for 15 minutes on any top-5 route for the pool
- 5xx + timeouts increase >= +0.5pp absolute sustained for 10 minutes
- OOM/CUDA error events > 0 in canary (Hosted internal pools) OR >= 3 events/hour in production pools
- Sustained queue saturation/backpressure: queue_depth_p95 >= configured_limit*0.9 for 10 minutes + associated timeouts
- Streaming instability: stream_disconnect_rate increase >= +0.3pp absolute sustained for 15 minutes

Soft rollback triggers (investigate for <= 60 minutes; rollback if not resolved):
- p95 latency regression >= +8% sustained for 30 minutes without compensating tokens/sec improvement
- tokens/sec regression >= -5% sustained for 30 minutes
- GPU memory headroom reduction >= 8% median across nodes (suggesting fragmentation/leaks) sustained for 60 minutes

Rollback steps (pool-level):
1) Flip per-pool override to disable hardware profiles (reverts to baseline defaults) without redeploy.
2) Confirm selected_profile metric drops to “none/baseline” and knob values match baseline.
3) If errors persist: roll back runtime image to previous stable release.
4) File incident + link graphs; open follow-ups against specific profile/preset change.

Post-rollback requirements:
- Capture effective config dump + selected_profile metrics + top affected routes
- Add/adjust perf-canary gate to prevent recurrence
- Update known-issues page if this is a new failure mode
comms_plan:
Audience + timing:
- eng-oncall + eng-sre: Send rollout heads-up 48 hours before Phase 1; update at each phase change; include rollback triggers and “kill switch” steps.
- Customer Support (SUP) + Solutions: Send enablement/triage notes 24 hours before Hosted ramp to 25%.
- Release channel (eng-releases): Post final go/no-go summary when moving from Phase 1 -> Phase 2.

Message must include:
- What is changing (profile pack + tuned presets), what is not changing (API surface, model behavior expectations)
- Where to monitor (dashboard links) + which metrics matter
- How to quickly disable per pool and how to verify it worked
- Known risks (tail latency trade-offs, long-context on L40S, B200 maturity)

Artifacts to link:
- Rollout runbook (Confluence)
- Perf-canary gates doc (Confluence)
- Known issues & mitigations page (Confluence)
- Debug endpoint / metrics doc (from pr-22027)
- CLI effective config dump instructions (from pr-22066)

release_checklist:
Pre-flight (must be complete before Phase 1):
- [ ] runtime-1.18 RC includes profile schema + validation (pr-21984) and selection logic (pr-21991)
- [ ] Override precedence tested in integration (pr-22047) and documented in ADR
- [ ] Selected profile + override source metrics shipped + dashboard panels updated (observability-pack/pr-488)
- [ ] Perf-canary gates merged and stable (perf-canary/pr-731); noise level acceptable (no >5% false positives week-over-week)
- [ ] H100 preset merged (pr-22003 + pr-22008) and tail latency regression fix included (pr-22033)
- [ ] L40S guardrails merged (pr-22015) and OOM repro no longer present in workload matrix run
- [ ] B200 experimental flag merged (pr-22021) + allowlist mechanism confirmed; B200 is default-off
- [ ] Startup logs print runtime/profile compatibility (pr-22041)
- [ ] CLI to dump effective config available (pr-22066)
- [ ] Runbook finalized: rollout + rollback steps, ownership, escalation (Confluence)
- [ ] Known issues page updated with current mitigations

Go/No-Go (day-of Phase 1):
- [ ] Perf-canary green on last 3 runs for each SKU/workload bucket
- [ ] Infra confirms pool has sufficient spare capacity for rollback without throttling
- [ ] SRE confirms alert routing and thresholds for the rollout window
- [ ] Release owner confirms revert plan for runtime image exists + tested
- [ ] Oncall acknowledges comms and knows kill switch steps

Post-rollout (after Phase 2 100%):
- [ ] Benchmark summary artifact attached to release notes (internal)
- [ ] Any waivers documented (what regressed, why acceptable, mitigation)
- [ ] Support playbook updated with troubleshooting steps + required logs
- [ ] Close the loop: update epic ENG-4821 with final outcomes and links

- Runtime (Exec sponsor): Mateo Alvarez — overall go/no-go for shipping in runtime-1.18
- Runtime Scheduling: Sofia Ivanova — scheduler preset safety and tail latency guardrails
- Runtime Kernels: Hiro Tanaka — kernel selection heuristics + known trade-offs documented
- Benchmarks: Claire Dubois — workload matrix coverage + methodology acceptance
- Infra/Fleet: Irene Choi — rollout tooling + pool targeting + capacity/rollback feasibility
- SRE: Neha Kapoor (delegate: Sean Gallagher) — rollback criteria, alerts, and oncall readiness
- Product (Rollouts/Rollback UX): Marissa Cole — customer-facing positioning and internal messaging alignment (expected behavior vs guarantees)

Note: B200 enabling outside internal pools requires separate explicit approval email/thread and cannot be covered by this baseline sign-off.
activity_log:
2025-12-06 (Talia Benson): Created ticket to consolidate release readiness items. Noted prior confusion during H100 canary about who owned the “disable per pool” switch; this ticket owns that clarity.

2025-12-09 (Connor O'Brien): Drafted phase-based rollout plan aligned with runtime-1.18 train. Added requirement that Dedicated rolls out on new nodes first.

2025-12-12 (Sean Gallagher): Requested numeric rollback triggers (no “SRE judgment calls”). Added hard/soft triggers and required monitoring windows.

2025-12-16 (Aisha Bello): Confirmed dashboards will segment by selected_profile; asked for final metric names (see pr-22027). Noted perf-canary thresholds still noisy for L40S runners.

2025-12-19 (Vanessa Ortiz): Confirmed pool targeting supports 5%/25%/50%/100% ramp for Hosted, but Dedicated is node-based. Added Dedicated plan accordingly.

2025-12-23 (Hiro Tanaka): Flagged that H100 throughput-first preset should not be default-on at launch; balanced preset is default, throughput-first is opt-in.

2026-01-03 (Neha Kapoor): Approved rollback criteria framework; requested explicit “OOM is zero tolerance in canary”. Added.

2026-01-07 (Mateo Alvarez): Approved B200 remains experimental and default-off. Requires separate go/no-go before any external rollout.

2026-01-09 (Connor O'Brien): Marked ticket In Review pending final Confluence runbook link updates and scheduled comms to eng-oncall + Support.
comments:
Open questions:
- Do we require an explicit “profile pack version pin” for Phase 1 even if runtime image is pinned? (Recommendation: yes, to reduce drift and ease rollback.)
- For Hosted ramp, is traffic splitting by route available everywhere, or only by pool? If only by pool, we need a plan to avoid over-weighting a single large customer.

Follow-ups (not blockers for release but should be tracked):
- Add automatic rollback playbook integration (single command) after 2 consecutive hard triggers.
- Expand workload matrix with more realistic tool-calling and streaming patterns (Applied ML request) and ensure gates cover it.
- Improve L40S perf-canary runner stability (see INT-8832).
